name: disk
title: A run changes hosts
claim: An agent reviews ten invoices in its workspace on an Archil disk. Midway, the run is released and a second sandbox opens it from the disk and finishes, with every payment made once.

keys.why: the review and report agents (google/gemini-3.8-flash at medium thinking); in a Daytona sandbox, the placeholder of a Daytona secret that holds the key, so the box never holds it
keys.where: aistudio.google.com, Get API key; for the sandbox, a Daytona secret (Daytona dashboard: Secrets) allowed for generativelanguage.googleapis.com only

keys.why: the run's directory and its claim live on an Archil disk; the demo mounts it, and creates and deletes run directories and token users on it
keys.where: the Archil console, in a SCRATCH organisation (never a production one): API keys

keys.why: the disk the run lives on (dsk-...)
keys.where: the Archil console, a disk in that scratch organisation that holds nothing else

keys.why: the disk's region; aws-us-east-1 when unset
keys.where: the Archil console, the disk's page

keys.why: the live kill deletes the Daytona sandbox the run is in, and the successor starts in a new one
keys.where: the Daytona dashboard: Keys, for an organisation on Tier 3 or 4 (the archil client needs full egress)

programs.why: runs the demo; Node 22.19 or later
the Archil client mounts the run's directory (0.8.42 or later)
FUSE, which the archil client mounts through (package fuse3)
this package's wrapper around the archil client, installed root-owned: the one command the run may run as root, through one sudoers line
